title: AI for wealth management: what are RIAs actually using it for?
description: AI for wealth management at RIAs: where it pays first, what AI notetakers cost and keep, the SEC rules that apply, and who signs off.
industry: wealth management and registered investment advisers
verdict: Most advisers now use AI, mainly for meeting notes, follow-up and drafting client emails.[^1][^2]
No AI-specific Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) rule exists; examiners apply existing duties on marketing, records and privacy.[^3][^4]
AI meeting notes can be required records, so check each tool's retention against the five-year rule.[^5][^6]
Advisors keep the client and the sign-off; most registered investment advisers (RIAs) plan to add advisors as AI frees time.[^7][^8]
Deepfake voice and video requests to move money are now a named SEC exam focus.[^9][^3]

onPage.text: Who signs off on notes, emails, advice and money movement
Six AI jobs at an RIA, ranked by payoff then effort
Our check of what advisor AI notetakers cost and what they keep
Adoption surveys, with who was actually asked
Where an advisor's week goes today
The SEC, FINRA, CFP Board and state rules that apply
Where it goes wrong, and the fix for each

headings.ranked: Where does AI pay first at an RIA or wealth firm?
headings.rules: Which rules apply to AI at an RIA?

headings.faq: Questions RIA leaders ask about AI

answers.human-role: Your advisors keep every recommendation and approve anything a client sees; the chief compliance officer owns retention and vendor review, and operations calls clients back before moving money.[^7][^12][^5][^17]
answers.ranked: AI pays first in meeting prep, notes and follow-up, where Kitces found over 11 hours a week of prep and follow-through; forms and client emails come next.[^19][^20][^10]
answers.rules: Your existing rules apply, since the SEC has no AI-specific rule: Advisers Act duties, the Marketing Rule, books and records Rule 204-2 and Regulation S-P.[^3][^4][^5][^15] FINRA rules also cover dual registrants, and CFP Board standards cover CFP professionals.[^49][^7]
answers.what-goes-wrong: AI goes wrong at RIAs through false AI claims, notes missing from the archive, deepfake money requests, unapproved tools and wrong plan math.[^44][^5][^9][^1][^13]
answers.something-else: Pick something else when your CRM or custodian already sells the AI job, when staff only need internal drafting, or when advisors need support staff more than software.[^35][^25][^39][^59]

summary: AI for wealth management drafts and summarizes advisor work: meeting notes, follow-up emails and review prep.[^2][^10] What changes is time: over half of advisers using AI save 4 or more hours a week.[^10] Advisors still own the advice, and AI notes can be required records.[^7][^5]
humanRole: Your team stays in charge of anything a client sees: the advisor edits AI notes and approves each follow-up before it goes.[^7] Vendors such as Jump build that approval step in (vendor claim).[^11]

The advisor makes every recommendation; AI gathers data and drafts options, and the fiduciary duty stays with the adviser.[^12] Planners check each figure, since tested models slip on multi-step financial math.[^13][^14]

The chief compliance officer (CCO) sets retention, reviews AI vendors and keeps the AI inventory.[^5][^15] Most firms already keep that inventory: 86% in the Investment Adviser Association (IAA) survey.[^16]
Operations releases money or changes an address only after calling the client back on a number already on file.[^17][^18] Deepfake voice and video requests are a named SEC exam focus.[^9]

ranked.name: Meeting prep, notes and follow-up
ranked.why: AI pays first in the hours around each meeting: Kitces found 5.3 hours of prep and 6 of follow-through a week.[^19] Notetakers are the top AI tool, used by 42.86% of advisors in T3's survey.[^2]
ranked.payoff: Advisor hours a week on prep and follow-up, before and after.

ranked.name: Customer relationship management (CRM) entry, forms and account opening
ranked.why: Vendors say 20-40% of paper account forms come back not in good order (NIGO).[^20][^21] One firm reports its NIGO rate fell from 35% to 11.5% after moving to digital forms.[^22]
ranked.payoff: NIGO rate on your own forms, and days from signed paperwork to a funded account.

ranked.name: Drafting client emails and letters
ranked.why: Among RIAs, 49% already use AI to draft client communications, per AssetMark's survey of 400 advisors.[^10] It is the top use worldwide too, at 51% in the Financial Planning Standards Board (FPSB) survey.[^23]
ranked.payoff: Minutes per client email, and compliance edits per draft.

ranked.name: Tax return and plan document review
ranked.why: A new financial plan takes about 18 hours, per the Kitces Report.[^24] Tools now read returns into checklists; Hazel lists a tax agent at $160 a month (vendor price).[^25]
ranked.payoff: Planner hours per new plan, and errors the planner catches.

ranked.name: Compliance surveillance and archive review
ranked.why: In the IAA survey, 60% of CCOs hold more than one role, and 72% of firms stepped up testing of AI use.[^16][^26] The SEC lists compliance monitoring and surveillance among the AI uses it is studying.[^3]
ranked.payoff: Share of captured messages reviewed each month, and hours per review.

ranked.name: Fraud checks on money movement
ranked.why: The SEC's 2027 exam priorities ask how firms prepare for AI phishing and deepfake voice and video.[^9][^3] Global regulators (IOSCO) and state regulators (NASAA) both warned about AI-enabled scams in 2026.[^27][^28]
ranked.payoff: Share of wire and address-change requests verified by callback.

ownData.title: What do advisor AI notetakers cost, and what do they keep?
ownData.intro: List prices run $39 to $184 per advisor a month, and kept transcripts range from 6 months to whatever the firm sets.[^29][^30][^31] We read each vendor's public pricing, security and FAQ pages on 26 Nov 2026; every cell is the vendor's own statement. For a 40-advisor firm, that is about $19,000 to $88,000 a year before add-ons (our arithmetic on list prices).

rules.name: Existing Advisers Act duties (no AI-specific SEC rule)
rules.status: In force; no AI rule as of 26 Nov 2026
rules.what: Your existing rules apply to AI; the SEC calls them technology-neutral obligations.[^3] It withdrew its 2023 predictive data analytics proposal on 12 Jun 2025.[^41][^42] A congressional report notes the SEC has issued no AI-specific rules.[^4]

rules.name: SEC Fiscal Year 2027 Examination Priorities
rules.what: Examiners will study AI use in research, drafting, client communications, portfolio management and surveillance.[^3] They will check readiness for AI phishing and deepfake voice and video.[^9] Law firms report requests for AI policies, training, disclosures and data security.[^43]

rules.name: Marketing Rule 206(4)-1, and Form ADV disclosures
rules.what: AI claims in your advertising must be true and backed by evidence; the SEC settled with three advisers over false AI claims in 2024.[^44][^45] Delphia's false claims also appeared in its Form ADV brochure, so check that too.[^46]

rules.name: Books and records Rule 204-2
rules.what: Written communications about advice are required records, kept 5 years, and the rule covers transcribed information of any type.[^5] Cooley suggests sorting AI notes into required and not required by category.[^6] Deleting a required record can itself be the violation.[^6]

rules.name: Regulation S-P amendments
rules.status: Larger firms from 3 Dec 2025; smaller from 3 Jun 2026
rules.what: You need an incident response program and oversight of service providers that handle customer data, AI vendors included.[^15][^47] Providers must tell you of a breach within 72 hours; affected customers get notice within 30 days.[^48]

rules.name: FINRA rules (dual registrants)
rules.what: The Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) says its rules are technology-neutral and apply to generative AI.[^49] Its 2026 report describes human review, logs of prompts and outputs, and model version tracking.[^50]

rules.name: CFP Board Standards and Generative AI Ethics Guide
rules.what: AI cannot replace a Certified Financial Planner (CFP) professional's care, skill, prudence and diligence, says the guide.[^7] Duties of care and confidentiality apply to each AI tool you use.[^51]

rules.name: NASAA and state regulators
rules.what: NASAA's adviser section is drafting guidance on AI disclosure, information safeguards, bias and conflicts.[^52] Its 2025 compliance note calls for strict human oversight of AI.[^53] State-registered advisers should watch for it.

watchOuts: AI goes wrong at RIAs in claims, records, fraud, unapproved tools and math, and false claims drew fines first.[^44][^45] The SEC fined Delphia $225,000 and Global Predictions $175,000; say only what your tools really do.[^46][^54]

Notes that never reach your archive: FinMate's page says it keeps transcripts 6 months, and required records are kept 5 years.[^31][^5] Check each tool's retention against Rule 204-2, and set exports to your archive before go-live.[^6]
Deepfake requests to move money or change an address, a named SEC exam focus.[^9][^27] Call the client back on a number already on file before acting, as the SEC warns of impersonators.[^17][^18]
Shadow AI: 82% of advisors who use AI experiment on their own, per Schwab.[^1] NASAA warns about client data in public tools; an acceptable use policy and an AI inventory are the fix.[^53][^16]

Wrong numbers in plans: in one benchmark, accuracy fell from over 90% on basic tasks to about 40% on complex ones.[^13] Leading models scored about 70% on personal finance questions, so a planner checks every figure.[^55]
Agents with too much reach: FINRA names autonomy, scope and auditability as agent risks.[^56][^50] Limit what an agent can touch, and log its prompts and outputs.[^50]

faq.q: Can advisors use ChatGPT with client data?
faq.a: Not on personal accounts; use a business plan whose terms bar training on your data and that your vendor review covers.[^15][^53] One r/CFP advisor said archiving needed an enterprise plan's compliance tools.[^57]

faq.q: Do AI meeting notes have to be archived?
faq.a: Yes, often: notes that record advice or client communications can be required records under Rule 204-2, kept 5 years.[^5] Cooley suggests deciding by category, with counsel.[^6]

faq.q: Do we have to record client meetings to use an AI notetaker?
faq.a: Not in one vendor's reading: Jump says neither Rule 204-2 nor FINRA Rule 4511(b) requires a recording.[^33] Advisors on r/CFP say some compliance teams approved tools because no audio is kept.[^57]
No sign of it yet: 73% of RIAs in a Cerulli study plan to add junior advisors as AI expands capacity.[^8] McKinsey projects a shortfall of about 100,000 advisors by 2034.[^58]

faq.q: Where should an RIA start with AI?
faq.a: Start with meeting notes for one team of advisors, since notetakers are the most-used AI tool.[^2] Set retention and archive exports first, then compare prep and follow-up hours before and after.[^6][^19]

faq.q: How much time does AI save financial advisors?
faq.a: Over half of AI adopters in AssetMark's survey of 400 advisors save 4 or more hours a week.[^10] McKinsey estimates generative AI could save 6-12% of advisor time.[^58]

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy first: tools for notes, CRM entry and drafting already list $39 to $184 per advisor a month.[^29][^30] Jump and Zocks name archive connections to Global Relay, Smarsh or Proofpoint.[^30][^32] Zavient's view: check the AI already in your CRM or custodian first.[^35][^25]
buyVsBuild.build: Zavient's view: build only where your data and workflow are the edge, such as onboarding across CRM, custodian and planning tools. Few firms have the data base for it: T3 found 3.27% use a data warehouse.[^2] Governance is the build every firm needs, and 86% of surveyed firms already have an AI policy.[^16]

pickElse: Pick something else when your CRM already sells the job: Wealthbox's AI Notetaker is a $49 add-on that keeps notes in the CRM (vendor claim).[^35][^36]
Your custodian already has AI: Hazel runs on Altruist, from $60 a month (vendor price).[^25]
Staff only need internal drafting and summaries: Microsoft 365 Copilot is a $21 a user add-on (standard price, read 26 Nov 2026).[^39]
Advisors are buried in admin and have no support staff: Kitces found support staff cut admin time more than technology did.[^59]

offer.heading: Which two AI jobs will your advisors actually keep using?
offer.body: Most likely meeting notes and client email drafts, since advisors already use AI for those most. In a free 30-minute call we map where advisor hours go, from meeting prep to forms and client emails. You leave knowing which tools fit your CRM and custodian, plus the retention, archive and vendor checks your CCO will ask for.

reviews.notes: COO of a 40-500 person RIA: the ranked list gives one job per line with a payoff to measure, and the human-role block names who signs off. Problem: SEC, RIA, CRM, IAA, FPSB, IOSCO, NASAA, FINRA and CFP were used before being spelled out, and SOC 2 was unexplained. Fixed: each spelled out on first use; the SOC 2 column now says it is a security audit. Also made the first line under each question heading answer it directly (summary, buy or build).

Head of operations: owns account opening and money movement. The callback control covered wires only; it now covers address changes too, in both the human-role and watch-out lines, matching FINRA's impersonation guidance. The NIGO payoff now says to measure on your own forms, because the 20-40% figures are vendor claims and the 35% to 11.5% drop is one firm's own case study, both labelled. Wanted archive connections spelled out per tool: the own-data table already has that column.

GM: wants to know if one team can pilot this and what it costs. Cost is answered by the dated notetaker price check and the 40-advisor yearly range. Swapped the 'what does the SEC look for' FAQ (already covered in the rules table) for 'Where should an RIA start with AI?': one advisor team on meeting notes, retention and archive exports set first, before-and-after hours. No Zavient price, per site rules.

Chief compliance officer / head of advisor operations: checks the exam angle. The Marketing Rule row mixed ads and Form ADV; it now says AI ad claims must be backed by evidence and flags Form ADV separately, as in the Delphia order. A human-role line cited the SEC press release for 'fiduciary duty stays with the firm'; now cited to the law-firm source that says it. Retention is stated neutrally: each vendor's own page against the rule text, with 'check it against Rule 204-2'; no vendor is called non-compliant. SEC naming: the page just says AI.

Owner-CEO: title and five bottom-line bullets answer the question in 10 seconds. Worries covered: client data (ChatGPT FAQ, Reg S-P), security (SOC 2 column, shadow AI), rules (rules table), cost (dated price check). His question after the vendor table was 'which one do I pick?'; the offer now promises tools that fit the CRM and custodian he already uses. Gap he will notice: no case from a firm his size beyond one firm's own NIGO case study, labelled; none is claimed. No price flagged, per Russell's 26 Nov decision.
